_comment: Phase 167.1.1.1 (BRIDGERETURNS) D-03, SC3. The cross-runtime oracle for the mark-price rule, spot and derivative. Read by analytics-service/tests/test_holding_marks_fixture.py (classify_spot_marks, classify_derivative_marks) and src/app/(dashboard)/compare/lib/holding-compare-adapter.test.ts (classifySpotMarks, classifyDerivativeMarks, analyzeSignedReturns, fetchHoldingCompareItem). HAND-TYPED: every expected figure was worked out by hand from the case's own marks (the arithmetic is in each case's why), never produced by either implementation. The rule: one mark per UTC day from the row with the latest updated_at instant, ties to the smallest LOWERCASE api_key_id; a finite mark at or below 0 is a gap skipped BEFORE that pick; a return exists only between two ADJACENT calendar days that both carry a mark, keyed by the LATER day; a spot holding needs min_priced_days priced days; the SPOT withheld ladder is account_balance, fixed_price (marks not read), then the read contract, then no_price, then too_few_priced_days. DERIVATIVE cases (holding_type derivative; D-02, D-10, D-12) are signed: a day direction is the single long or short value shared by ALL rows of that day (gap-mark rows and every key included); a flat row or mixed sides leave the day with NO direction, a gap; the return from day i-1 to day i carries DAY i-1 direction and exists only between adjacent days that BOTH have a positive mark and a direction; r = s(i-1) * (p_i / p_(i-1) - 1), s = +1 long and -1 short, floored at -1.0; priced_days counts usable days; the DERIVATIVE ladder is option_premium (symbol only, marks not read), the read contract (side must be long, short or flat), no_price, no_direction, too_few_priced_days. ts_nav (optional) is what the TypeScript analyzeSignedReturns must give for the case returns. ts maps a SPOT case onto what /compare shows; derivative cases are not mapped there until plan 07 wires /compare. Do not add a case here without both runtimes consuming it; the two suites read this file whole.

cases.name: purchase_at_constant_mark
cases.why: SC1: the mark never moves while the quantity and the dollar value do; the dollar-ratio read printed +100% and -75%, the price rule must print exactly 0.

cases.name: latest_updated_at_wins
cases.why: D-03: three keys on day 2; the row with the latest updated_at instant (key-b, 11:00Z, mark 102) wins. It sits in the MIDDLE of the input so neither first-row-wins nor last-row-wins passes. Return = 102/100 - 1 = 0.02.

cases.name: tie_to_smallest_lowercase_key
cases.why: D-03: the same instant written two ways (Z and +00:00 with a six-digit fraction). Tie goes to the smallest LOWERCASE api_key_id: key-a (mark 104) beats Key-B (mark 103), although a raw compare would put the capital K first. Return = 104/100 - 1 = 0.04.

cases.name: zero_mark_never_eclipses
cases.why: D-03: a LATER row with mark 0 (the failed-ticker sentinel) is a gap skipped BEFORE the pick, so the earlier valid 105 stands. Return = 105/100 - 1 = 0.05.

cases.name: negative_mark_is_a_gap
cases.why: D-03: a negative mark is a gap (day 2 unpriced), so days 1 and 3 are priced but not adjacent: 2 priced days, no return.

cases.name: missing_day_breaks_chain
cases.why: D-03: days 1, 2 and 4. Only day 2 follows an adjacent priced day; day 4 follows a gap and carries no return. Return day 2 = 110/100 - 1 = 0.1.

cases.name: real_path
cases.why: D-03: marks 100, 110, 99 on adjacent days. Returns 110/100 - 1 = 0.1 (keyed day 2) and 99/110 - 1 = -0.1 (keyed day 3).

cases.name: spot_flat_side_is_not_a_gap
cases.why: Spot rows carry side flat (PROD: every spot row). The spot rule never reads side, so flat is not a gap. Marks 50, 55, 60.5: returns 0.1 and 0.1.

cases.name: twenty_nine_priced_days
cases.why: SC2 boundary: 29 adjacent priced days is one short. Withheld too_few_priced_days; priced_days 29 and all 28 returns still reported. Marks alternate 100 / 200: even days return 1.0, odd days -0.5.

cases.name: thirty_priced_days
cases.why: SC2 boundary: 30 priced days is enough. Withheld null; priced_days 30 and 29 returns.

cases.name: stablecoin_usdt
cases.why: SC2: a stablecoin symbol is a writer constant: fixed_price. The marks are not read (one is a string).

cases.name: lowercase_usdc
cases.why: SC2: symbol match is case-insensitive.

cases.name: sfox_any_symbol
cases.why: SC2: sFOX writes mark_price 1.0 for every row it keeps, so any symbol on sfox is fixed_price; the venue match is case-insensitive.

cases.name: mt5_account
cases.why: SC2: a venue that is not a crypto exchange is an account balance whatever the symbol, tested BEFORE fixed_price (a USDT symbol on mt5 is account_balance, not fixed_price).

cases.name: all_zero_marks
cases.why: SC2: rows exist but no day carries a valid mark (the 0.0 sentinel on every day): no_price, not too_few_priced_days.

cases.name: contract_mark_string
cases.why: Read contract: a string mark is a violation, never a gap.

cases.name: contract_mark_bool
cases.why: Read contract: a boolean mark is a violation (a bool is an int in Python).

cases.name: contract_mark_null
cases.why: Read contract: a null mark is a violation.

cases.name: contract_asof_not_padded
cases.why: Read contract: an asof that is not zero-padded YYYY-MM-DD is a violation.

cases.name: contract_asof_impossible_date
cases.why: Read contract: 2026-02-30 matches the shape but is not a real date; Python and JavaScript would otherwise disagree on it.

cases.name: updated_at_unparseable
cases.why: A positive-mark row with an unusable updated_at cannot be ordered: HoldingsUpdatedAtError, not a silent pick.

cases.name: worked_example_long
cases.why: D-02 worked example (RESEARCH Q4), all rows long, marks 100, 110, 100 on adjacent days. Returns +110/100-1 = 0.1 (keyed day 2) and 100/110-1 = -1/11 = -0.0909090909090909 (day 3). NAV 1.1 then 1.0: cumulative 0, max drawdown (1.0-1.1)/1.1 = -1/11.

cases.name: worked_example_short
cases.why: D-02 worked example (RESEARCH Q4), the same marks 100, 110, 100 with every row short: each return is the long return negated. Returns -0.1 (day 2) and +1/11 = 0.0909090909090909 (day 3). NAV 0.9 then 0.9*(12/11) = 0.981818...: cumulative -0.0181818181818182, max drawdown (0.9-1)/1 = -0.1.

cases.name: flip_day_before_governs
cases.why: D-12 interval rule: marks 100, 110, 121 with sides long, short, short. The return INTO day 2 carries day 1 direction (long): +0.1. The return into day 3 carries day 2 direction (short): -(121/110-1) = -0.1. Signing by the later day would give -0.1 and -0.1. NAV 1.1 then 1.1*0.9 = 0.99: cumulative -0.01, max drawdown (0.99-1.1)/1.1 = -0.1.

cases.name: flat_day_is_a_gap
cases.why: D-02/D-12: day 2 is flat, so it has no direction and is a gap, never a guessed sign. Neither interval touching day 2 exists, and days 1 and 3 are not adjacent: 2 usable days, no return.

cases.name: flat_day_does_not_kill_later_chain
cases.why: D-12: a flat day 2 removes the intervals 1-2 and 2-3 only. Day 3 (121, long) to day 4 (133.1, long) is adjacent with both days usable: 133.1/121 - 1 = 0.1. 3 usable days.

cases.name: mixed_sides_day_is_a_gap
cases.why: D-02: on day 2 key-a is long and key-b is short, so the day has no direction (never the majority, never the latest). Days 1 and 3 are usable but not adjacent: 2 usable days, no return.

cases.name: gap_mark_row_still_votes
cases.why: D-02: the direction comes from ALL rows of the day, including a row whose mark is a gap. Day 2: key-a mark 0 (gap) side long, key-b mark 105 side short, so the sides are mixed and day 2 is unusable. Were the gap row ignored, day 2 would read short and two returns would exist. 2 usable days, no return.

cases.name: two_keys_agree_pick_latest
cases.why: D-02: two keys both short on day 2 give a short day; the mark is the latest updated_at (key-b 91 beats key-a 90), as the spot pick does. Returns: day 2 -(91/100-1) = +0.09; day 3 -(100/91-1) = -9/91 = -0.0989010989010989.

cases.name: all_flat_with_prices
cases.why: D-03 ladder: positive marks exist but every day is flat, so no day is usable: no_direction (not no_price, not too_few_priced_days).

cases.name: all_marks_non_positive
cases.why: D-03 ladder: every mark is a gap (0, -1, 0), so no day carries a price: no_price, whatever the sides.

cases.name: option_put_deribit
cases.why: D-10: a Deribit name ending -P is an option, withheld as option_premium. The marks are NOT read (one is a string, which would be a contract error on any other holding).

cases.name: option_lowercase
cases.why: D-10: the name is matched case-insensitively, so a lowercase -c is an option.

cases.name: option_linear
cases.why: D-10: a linear-margin option name (ETH_USDC-27MAR26-50000-C) is an option too; the underscore margin marker does not make it spot.

cases.name: not_option_perp
cases.why: D-10: BTC-PERPETUAL is not an option. Classified by marks 100, 110, 121 all long: returns +0.1 and 121/110-1 = +0.1.

cases.name: not_option_linear_perp
cases.why: D-10: 1000PEPEUSDT is a linear perpetual, not an option. All short, marks 100, 90, 99: day 2 -(90/100-1) = +0.1; day 3 -(99/90-1) = -0.1.

cases.name: short_over_150pct_spike
cases.why: D-12 / OQ-5: a short whose mark goes 1.0 to 2.5 is -(2.5/1.0-1) = -1.5 unfloored; the floor makes it -1.0 (a holder cannot lose more than the position). NAV 0: cumulative -1.0, max drawdown (0-1)/1 = -1.0.

cases.name: twenty_nine_usable_days
cases.why: SC2 boundary for derivatives: 30 days carry a positive mark but day 30 is flat, so only 29 are USABLE: too_few_priced_days with priced_days 29 (usable days, not priced days). 28 returns (none touches day 30): marks alternate 100 / 125, long, even days 125/100-1 = 0.25, odd days 100/125-1 = -0.2.

cases.name: thirty_usable_days
cases.why: SC2 boundary for derivatives: 30 usable short days, marks alternate 100 / 125: eligible (withheld null), priced_days 30, 29 returns. Short negates: even days -(125/100-1) = -0.25, odd days -(100/125-1) = +0.2.

cases.name: empty_signed_returns
cases.why: 30 usable long days every second day (Jan 1, 3, ... 31, Feb 2, 4, ... 28): eligible with priced_days 30 but NO two days are adjacent, so there are no returns. The NAV metrics of an empty list are null, never a confident 0%.

cases.name: bad_side
cases.why: Read contract: a side outside long, short, flat is a violation (bad_sides), never a gap.

cases.name: null_side
cases.why: Read contract: a null side on a derivative row is a violation, never a gap.
